questions.question: Explain, step by step, how you would decide which of R1 850, R1 580 and R1 805 is the largest amount.
questions.expected_answer: All three have four digits and all have 1 thousand, so compare the hundreds: 8, 5 and 8. The 5 is smallest, so R1 580 is the smallest. R1 850 and R1 805 both have 8 hundreds, so compare the tens: 5 and 0. R1 850 has more tens, so R1 850 is the largest.

questions.question: Write 2 502 and 1 085 in words and in expanded form, and explain what the zeros mean.
questions.expected_answer: 2 502 is two thousand five hundred and two, expanded as 2 000 plus 500 plus 0 plus 2; the zero means there are no tens. 1 085 is one thousand and eighty-five, expanded as 1 000 plus 0 plus 80 plus 5; the zero means there are no hundreds, so no hundreds word is spoken.

questions.question: Explain the quick test for odd and even numbers and use it on 346, 1 085 and 1 000.
questions.expected_answer: Look only at the last digit. If it is 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8 the number is even; if it is 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9 the number is odd. 346 ends in 6, so it is even. 1 085 ends in 5, so it is odd. 1 000 ends in 0, so it is even.
